outro.line: Save this before your next launch day

hook.title: My whole app from *one* prompt. *2,000* lines. *Launch* Saturday.

beats.text: My whole app came from one prompt. Two thousand lines. Launch is Saturday.
Another prompt will make it worse. Not better.
How many prompts did it take?
One. Okay, eleven. Mostly "fix it."
Scroll up. Your chat says forty-one.
Forty-one. Nobody's read any of it. Including me.
Step one. Turn on plan mode before any code.

panel.title: Plan mode first
panel.html:
~/my-app $ claude
Plan mode: on. No edits yet.
you: just build it all
Plan: first feature only.

beats.text: A plan? I wanted the app.
Plans are free. Rewrites are not.
Step two. Ask what every file does, in plain English.

panel.title: Explain every file
panel.html:
JSapp.js
app.js: the screen you see first.
db.js: saves every signup.

beats.text: I don't know what half of them do.
Good. That's the part you skipped.
Step three. One feature per prompt. Not the whole app.

panel.title: One feature at a time
panel.html:
add login, payments and emails
3 features1 feature
Start with login. Test it first.

beats.text: But the payments are the whole point.
Then they're tomorrow's problem.
Step four. Test it, then save a copy before the next feature.

panel.title: Save before you add more
panel.html:
✓ login test passed
git commit -m "login works"
Saved. Next feature: payments.

beats.text: So I launch Saturday with one feature?
One feature that works. Yes.
Fine. I read all 2,000 lines.
Start with file one. There are sixty-one.
Okay. Launch is Monday then.
Plan mode already said Monday.
